Activate theme_mt() as the session's default theme

Source: R/theme.R
use_theme_mt.Rd

Calls ggplot2::theme_set() with theme_mt(base_size = base_size) and sets geom_density()'s default adjust to 5 (a heavier smoothing bandwidth than ggplot2's own default, matching how geom_density() is used throughout this package's plots). Call this once per session/script after library(emptyviz) - loading the package does not do this automatically, since a package silently mutating global ggplot2 state on load is a bad default.

Usage

use_theme_mt(base_size = 10, ...)

Arguments

base_size

Passed to theme_mt().

...

Passed to theme_mt() as well - e.g. base_family or dark, for callers that want an activated theme other than the plain default.

Value

invisible(NULL), called for its side effect.

Details

If knitr is installed, this also registers a knit_print method for ggplot/patchwork objects that renders a chunk twice - once normally, once with a dark-mode color overlay - whenever that chunk sets the dual_render chunk option to TRUE (directly, or via a project-wide knitr: opts_chunk: dual_render: true default), emitting both images wrapped for Quarto's light/dark toggle. Chunks that don't set the option are completely unaffected.

See also

theme_mt()

Examples

old <- ggplot2::theme_get() # so the example can restore it afterward
use_theme_mt()
ggplot2::theme_set(old) # not required in a real script/session
